title: Interactive proofs of quantumness

problem.name: Interactive proofs of quantumness
problem.statement_latex: A classical verifier supplies a public key for a trapdoor claw-free pair $(f_{k,0},f_{k,1})$. The prover commits to an image $y$, then answers a random challenge with a preimage or a prescribed measurement relation between its two preimages. The objective is an acceptance probability above the efficient-classical-prover threshold. Complexity uses gates, communication, and security parameter $\lambda$.

quantum.headline_latex: $\operatorname{poly}(\lambda)$ prover gates and verifier time. Coherent function evaluation and image measurement retain a superposition of the two preimages. BCMVV uses complementary-basis challenges. The computational Bell protocol achieves $p_x=1$ and $p_{\rm CHSH}=\cos^2(\pi/8)$; Rabin-function implementations use modular squaring.
quantum.headline_text: $\operatorname{poly}(\lambda)$ prover gates and verifier time. Coherent function evaluation and image measurement retain a superposition of the two preimages. BCMVV uses complementary-basis challenges. The computational Bell protocol achieves $p_x=1$ and $p_{\rm CHSH}=\cos^2(\pi/8)$; Rabin-function implementations use modular squaring.

classical.headline_latex: Under claw-freeness, classical polynomial-time provers satisfy $p_x+4p_{\rm CHSH}-4\leq\operatorname{negl}(\lambda)$. For the factoring-based instantiation, factoring the $\lambda$-bit modulus gives an attack with heuristic number-field-sieve time $\exp(O(\lambda^{1/3}(\log\lambda)^{2/3}))$. The LWE instantiation uses its lattice-attack parameters and adaptive-hardcore-bit assumption.
